verdict.rationale: Name.com documents a public Core API with HTTP Basic authentication, API tokens, and reference endpoints for domain registration, availability checks, DNS records, transfers, email forwarding, WHOIS privacy and webhook subscriptions. It also offers official SDKs and a sandbox environment, and a probe confirms machine-readable docs via llms.txt. missing for 10: a discoverable OpenAPI/Swagger spec (probe paths returned 404), independent hands-on corroboration of API usage.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can drive the product through a documented public API

citations.quote: The Core API uses **HTTP Basic Authentication** with your name.com API credentials.

Registers a new domain under your account. You must provide `domain.domainName` at minimum. This endpoint is commonly used to programmatically onboard new domains through user signup flows or checkout experiences.
Adds a new DNS record to the specified domain zone. Provide the record type (e.g. A, MX, CNAME), host, value, and TTL.
Official client SDKs for the name.com Core API. They give you typed clients that map directly to the API reference
Go to Account Settings → Security → API Tokens and issue both development and production tokens
